statement: Cat admits the cardinal filtration Cat^pi of categories with at most pi arrows, for infinite pi.

statement: Filtered colimits commute with pullback in Cat and in presheaf categories.

statement: Effective unions of subobjects may fail in Cat.

notes: Source expresses doubt; modern status here is a proved finite counterexample, not open.

repair: Push out [1] into its groupoid completion against the finite category with ba=ca but b unequal c; inverting a identifies b and c. Fully proved at p102.

statement: i_A preserves filtered colimits, hence W_A is filtered-colimit closed if W is.

statement: Loc(1a): every isomorphism belongs to W.

repair: Two-out-of-three; in particular identities and this clause give closure under composition.

statement: Loc(1bis): Loc(1) plus closure under retracts in the arrow category of Cat.
repair: Retracts refer to commutative squares with a retraction, not merely retracts of objects.

statement: Loc(2): a category with a terminal object is W-aspherical, meaning its map to e belongs to W.
repair: This includes the empty-category exclusion implicit in having a terminal object.

repair: This is the weak or absolute Theorem A condition; do not replace it silently by relative Theorem A.

statement: Under Loc(1,2), X/y is W-aspherical if and only if X/y→Y/y belongs to W.
repair: Y/y has terminal object (y,1_y), so two-out-of-three proves the equivalence.

repair: Comma categories are not generally strict fibres. This relative condition is used in modern fundamental localizers.

statement: Loc(3bis) should suffice when tested only on split fibred categories and split cartesian morphisms, assuming Loc(1,2).
gap_or_error: The parenthetical sauf erreur supplies no reduction or fibration convention.

gap_or_error: This contains reverse excision, stronger than ordinary pushout stability of weak homotopy equivalences.

statement: An old W-fibration X→Y is tested by pullback along maps between contractible categories over Y.
repair: Separate this local transport condition from intrinsic Fib_W, which requires preservation of every W-map under pullback.

statement: Loc(6a): every old W-fibration belongs to intrinsic Fib_W.
repair: This is the strongest displayed fibration condition; the original XII notation is W(4a).

statement: Loc(6a′): the pullback-preservation assertion is restricted to Parf_ω.

statement: Footnote 44 reserves the unused label Loc(5) for a more basic later axiom.
